source.citation: Dwivedi-Yu T, Baniecki ML, Toh E, et al. (2023) Selective whole-genome amplification reveals population genetics of Leishmania braziliensis directly from patient skin biopsies. PLOS Pathogens 19(3):e1011230.
source.tables: S1 Table (ppat.1011230.s004.xlsx): sheet 1 gives all 23 primers with set membership, sheet 2 gives the four assembled sets. Outcomes quoted from Results.
source.notes: Outcomes are categorical - the paper reports which sets worked, not a per-set enrichment figure. PS1 and PS4 reached >=60% parasite-mapping reads from 1% and 0.1% starting parasite DNA; PS2 and PS3 'performed more poorly on synthetic samples' and were only used in nested second-round reactions after PS1 or PS4. Across 66 patient samples the workflow succeeded on 18 (27%), with median 86.6% of the genome at >=10x and 38x median coverage. This is the only set in the suite designed against MULTIPLE backgrounds, and the only one using 8-mers against a GC-rich (~60%) target.
